edges.description: Loss of membrane-targeted connexins reduces the capacity of keratinocytes to form effective epidermal gap junctions.
Loss of effective epidermal gap-junction communication disrupts the differentiation programs that normally maintain cutaneous homeostasis.
Disturbed epidermal homeostasis produces episodic figurate erythematous patches.
Abnormal keratinization produces persistent hyperkeratotic plaques.
Palmoplantar epidermal keratinization defects manifest as palmoplantar keratoderma.
Deficient epidermal ceramide synthesis produces the scaly hyperkeratotic phenotype. The steps between the enzymatic defect and the epidermal lesion are not characterized in the reporting study.
Keratinocytes overexpressing either mutant channel proliferate more than controls, so channel hyperactivity drives the proliferative state.

Immature desmosomes and impaired adhesion accompany the widespread erythrokeratoderma of EKVP7. The reporting authors state that the exact function of PERP in desmosomes is unknown, so the intervening steps are not established.
Increased keratinocyte proliferation accompanies the up-regulation of proliferation and differentiation markers seen in affected skin, and contributes to the hyperkeratotic phenotype.

Loss of keratin 83 co-segregates with the progressive symmetric erythrokeratoderma phenotype. The authors' own conclusion is hedged to "at least some cases", and no intervening epidermal mechanism is reported.

nodes.description: Impaired epidermal differentiation and homeostasis, producing persistent hyperkeratosis and episodic erythematous lesions. This is the convergence point of every subtype in the entry: the connexin subtypes reach it through failed gap-junction communication, and the non-connexin subtypes reach it through deficient ceramide synthesis, desmosome immaturity, keratinocyte hyperproliferation, or loss of keratin 83.

evidence.snippet: Our results implicate Cx31 in the pathogenesis of EKV, and provide evidence that intercellular communication mediated by Cx31 is crucial for epidermal differentiation and response to external factors.

evidence.snippet: These findings reveal a critical role for Cx43 in epidermal homeostasis, and they provide evidence of organ-specific pathobiology resulting from different mutations within GJA1.

nodes.description: Pathogenic EKV variants disrupt connexin trafficking or membrane localization, preventing normal delivery of epidermal connexins to the cell surface. Mislocalization has been shown for all three connexin genes of the EKVP series - Cx31 (GJB3), Cx30.3 (GJB4) and Cx43 (GJA1) - so this node is the shared entry point of the connexin subtypes EKVP1 to EKVP3.

nodes.description: The EKVP7 route. Skin from a subject homozygous for the N-terminal PERP truncation shows desmosomes lacking the electron-dense midline of mature desmosomes, with reduced desmosome numbers and increased fragmentation after mechanical stress, while other desmosomal components localize normally. The exact function of PERP within the desmosome is not known.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in PERP Cause Dominant and Recessive Keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Both exhibit epidermal hyperproliferation, immature desmosomes lacking a dense midline observed via electron microscopy, and impaired intercellular adhesion upon mechanical stress.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in PERP Cause Dominant and Recessive Keratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Localization of other desmosomal components appears normal, which is in contrast to other conditions caused by mutations in genes encoding desmosomal proteins.

nodes.description: The EKVP4 route. KDSR catalyses a step of the ceramide synthesis pathway, and the reported biallelic EKVP4 alleles were shown by immunohistochemistry and yeast complementation to impair KDSR function. Ceramide output is therefore reduced rather than merely altered - an inference the isotretinoin response supports, since the authors read it as recruitment of alternative pathways for ceramide generation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in KDSR Cause Recessive Progressive Symmetric Erythrokeratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Immunohistochemistry and yeast complementation studies demonstrated that the mutations cause defects in KDSR function.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in KDSR Cause Recessive Progressive Symmetric Erythrokeratoderma.
evidence.snippet: Systemic isotretinoin therapy has achieved nearly complete resolution in the two probands in whom it has been applied, consistent with the effects of retinoic acid on alternative pathways for ceramide generation.

nodes.description: The EKVP5 route, and the least characterized. The single reported kindred carries a homozygous KRT83 frameshift that the authors state is expected to abolish keratin 83, a type II keratin of hair and skin. That expectation is the whole of the molecular claim available, so this node records a predicted null and asserts nothing about how it reaches the epidermis.

nodes.description: Increased keratinocyte proliferation, reported for both non-connexin dominant and recessive routes in this entry: keratinocytes overexpressing either mutant TRPM4 channel show enhanced proliferation, and skin from both the dominant and recessive PERP subjects is hyperproliferative. Only TRPM4 carries a downstream edge into this node. The PERP route reaches it through the gene binding alone, because the PERP report establishes that the skin is hyperproliferative without establishing whether that follows the desmosome maturation failure or accompanies it.

Both reported alleles sit in the S6 transmembrane domain, where the cryo-EM structures predict a direct effect on activation gating, and electrophysiology of the mutants shows raised baseline activity, greater sensitivity to intracellular Ca2+ and a higher resting membrane potential.
